description: Aerospace Village focuses on aviation and space cybersecurity, covering satellite communication, avionics architectures, and flight systems security. Talks explore vulnerabilities in avionics protocols, satellite tracking and simulation, GPS and RF spoofing, and collaborative disclosure across the aerospace ecosystem.

talks.title: What I Learned Trying to Hack a 737
talks.teaser: Examines the architecture and security design of Boeing 737 Communication Management Units through embedded reverse engineering.
talks.summary:
Reverse Engineering Avionics Hardware

Communication Management Units (CMUs) aboard Boeing 737 aircraft handle critical communications and operational telemetry between flight systems and ground networks. Reverse engineering two separate CMU models reveals unique hardware architectures distinct from standard commercial embedded systems.

Certification and Design Assurance Levels

Avionics systems require certification to strict Design Assurance Level (DAL) safety criteria under FAA and international airworthiness standards. These safety baselines prevent faults from propagating into flight control systems or disrupting cockpit communication channels.

Balancing Safety with Custom Airline Software

Commercial airlines routinely require custom airline operational communications (AOC) applications to manage passenger logistics, flight dispatching, and engine health reporting. Aircraft manufacturers address these competing needs by isolating certified baseline firmware from airline-specific software environments.

Embedded Architecture and Flight Isolation

An examination of 737 CMU internal architectures demonstrates how systems partition network domains, manage shared bus lines, and enforce strict boundary controls across operational avionics.

talks.title: Understanding Space Through a Cybersecurity Lens
talks.teaser: Provides an architectural overview of space mission design, spacecraft lifecycle constraints, and technical trade-offs across the space industry.
talks.summary:
Foundations of Space Mission Design

Space systems operate under rigorous physical and programmatic constraints that govern the entire lifecycle of satellites and launch vehicles from inception to decommissioning.

Spacecraft Architecture and Orbital Mechanics

Designing space missions requires navigating complex trade-offs between payload capacity, propulsion, power generation, thermal management, and reliable telemetry links.

Operational and Cybersecurity Trade-Offs

Mission planners must evaluate ground station connectivity, orbital dynamics, and space environment hazards when architecting communications and flight computers for long-duration operations.

Analyzing Technical and Programmatic Constraints

Synthesizing space engineering concepts provides technical practitioners with frameworks to evaluate spacecraft subsystem vulnerabilities, ground station exposure, and mission assurance risks.

talks.title: Trust and Truth in SSA
talks.teaser: Examines how malicious manipulation of centralized Space Situational Awareness collision data can mislead satellite operators.
talks.summary:
The Role of Space Situational Awareness

Space Situational Awareness (SSA) data tracks tens of thousands of orbital debris objects and active satellites to calculate conjunction assessments and prevent catastrophic collisions in orbit.

Centralized Data Repositories and Trust Dynamics

Due to the immense radar and optical sensing infrastructure required to monitor orbital paths, most satellite operators rely on centralized third-party repositories for conjunction alerts and ephemeris tracking.

Threat Modeling SSA Data Manipulation

A determined attacker targeting SSA data feeds can alter conjunction projections, either concealing genuine collision risks or injecting falsified warnings to force unnecessary collision-avoidance maneuvers.

Simulating Orbital Conjunction Attacks

Simulated attack scenarios illustrate how subtle modifications to tracking data can induce satellite owners to burn vital fuel reserves, degrade operational lifespans, or shift orbits into hostile positions.

Defenses and Data Verification

Mitigating data tampering requires verifiable telemetry feeds, multi-source sensor aggregation, and cryptographic authentication between tracking radars, orbital catalog operators, and satellite operations centers.

talks.title: TCAS and ILS Spoofing Demonstration
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how spoofed TCAS and ILS signals can induce automated autopilot climb or descent responses on commercial aircraft.
talks.summary:
Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance Architecture

The Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS) interrogates Mode S and Mode C transponders of nearby aircraft to compute relative distance, bearing, and altitude for collision detection.

Automated Autopilot Resolution Advisories

When a collision trajectory is calculated, TCAS issues a Resolution Advisory (RA). Certain modern autopilots automatically couple to the RA, commanding climbs or descents without manual pilot stick inputs.

Spoofing RF Transponder Signals

Transponder communications lack cryptographic authentication, enabling software-defined radios to synthesize arbitrary phantom aircraft tracks and broadcast deceptive interrogations and replies.

Impact on Flight Management and Aircraft Control

Testing simulated and avionics hardware responses reveals how false TCAS targets can compel autopilot flight directors into uncommanded flight level deviations during critical flight regimes.

talks.title: Talking to Satellites
talks.teaser: Shows how to configure low-cost amateur radio equipment and handheld antennas to establish two-way satellite communications.
talks.summary:
Accessible Satellite Communications

Direct communication with orbiting satellites does not require institutional earth stations or massive budgets, but can be accomplished using inexpensive amateur radio equipment.

Hardware and Equipment Selection

A functional satellite ground station can be assembled for approximately one hundred dollars using handheld dual-band transceivers, directional Yagi antennas, and basic software tools.

Tracking Orbital Passes and Doppler Shift

Establishing contact with low Earth orbit amateur satellites requires tracking pass schedules, calculating line-of-sight elevation angles, and adjusting frequencies in real time for Doppler shift.

Operating Across Transponders and Repeaters

Using amateur satellite repeaters enables radio operators to relay voice and data packets across thousands of miles, demonstrating accessible aerospace RF fundamentals.

talks.title: Software Defined Radios for Aerospace Cyber
talks.teaser: Explores the application of software-defined radios for analyzing and testing RF communications across aerospace cyber environments.
talks.summary:
In this accessible presentation from the DEF CON Safe Mode Aerospace Village, the speaker introduces attendees to the fundamentals of Software Defined Radios (SDRs) and their applications in aerospace cybersecurity. Opening at 00:06, the presenter outlines how affordable radio hardware has democratized RF exploration for researchers and hobbyists.

At 01:00, the talk covers essential radio frequency concepts, including carrier frequencies, bandwidth allocation, and signal modulation. At 02:02, the speaker demonstrates setting up an entry-level RTL-SDR dongle paired with a dedicated 1090 MHz antenna to intercept Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) signals emitted by commercial aircraft.

At 03:01 and 04:12, the demonstration highlights tuning into live frequencies using software packages like GQRX and dump1090. The presenter shows how to read spectral waterfall displays and decode live transponder telemetry, providing a practical foundation for analyzing aerospace radio communications. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Simulated Satellite Communications on Raspberry Pi
talks.teaser: Walks through building a CubeSat Simulator Lite using a Raspberry Pi and software-defined radio to transmit mock satellite telemetry.
talks.summary:
Hands-On Satellite Hardware Simulation

The CubeSat Simulator Lite project provides an accessible entry point into aerospace cybersecurity by emulating the digital and RF subsystems of an operational nanosatellite.

Building the Raspberry Pi Ground Node

The workshop setup configures a Raspberry Pi single-board computer running dedicated software packages to generate sensor telemetry, including battery voltage, temperature, and simulated altitude data.

Transmitting and Decoding Satellite Signals

Attaching a small antenna to the Pi allows it to broadcast digital telemetry frames over amateur radio bands, which participants capture and demodulate using software-defined radios.

Educational Applications in Aerospace Security

Simulating small satellite payloads provides security researchers with a safe, repeatable hardware environment to study telemetry formatting, frame encoding, and space communication link vulnerabilities.

talks.title: Satellite Orbits 101
talks.teaser: Demystifies orbital mechanics, launch windows, altitude classifications, and inclination parameters for space mission tracking.
talks.summary:
Principles of Orbital Mechanics

Reaching and maintaining stable orbit requires balancing gravitational pull with orbital velocity, governed by fundamental physical laws and vehicle energy states.

Orbital Classifications and Altitudes

Spacecraft operate in varied orbital regimes, ranging from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) with rapid orbital periods to High Earth Orbit (HEO) and geosynchronous trajectories tailored for persistent coverage.

Inclination, Eccentricity, and Launch Trajectories

Orbital characteristics depend heavily on launch site latitude and azimuth windows. Launches from equatorial sites gain rotational velocity assistance for equatorial orbits, while polar launches require dedicated energy profiles.

Visualizing Spacecraft Behaviors

Using orbital tracking and visualization tools allows analysts to predict satellite ground tracks, antenna look angles, and solar illumination cycles essential for space operations.

talks.title: Secure Airplane Development Lifecycle
talks.teaser: Outlines Boeing's product security framework for integrating cyber resiliency into commercial airplane design and verification.
talks.summary:
The E-Enabled Aircraft Attack Surface

Modern commercial aircraft integrate networked avionics, maintenance data links, and in-cabin connectivity, requiring the aviation industry to expand its historic safety focus to address intentional cyber threats.

Boeing Product Security Framework

Boeing Commercial Airplanes established dedicated product security programs to embed cyber resiliency across every stage of commercial aircraft conception, design, and manufacturing.

Integrating Security into the Development Lifecycle

The Secure Airplane Development Lifecycle embeds threat modeling, attack surface evaluations, and rigorous verification testing into traditional system engineering and certification gates.

Verifying Cyber Resiliency in Commercial Aviation

Ensuring long-term fleet resilience involves verifying software integrity, enforcing domain isolation between flight controls and passenger domains, and establishing robust incident response processes.

talks.title: Opening Remarks
talks.teaser: Welcomes attendees to the DEF CON Safe Mode Aerospace Village and outlines the event schedule, challenges, and tracks.
talks.summary:
Aerospace Village Director Pete Cooper delivers the opening remarks for the DEF CON Safe Mode Aerospace Village, welcoming global attendees and charting the ongoing expansion of the aviation and aerospace cybersecurity discipline [00:05, 00:11].

Cooper explores the accelerating digitization of flight and space infrastructure, explaining how modern avionics, satellite constellations, and ground control systems increasingly intersect with internet-connected networks and commercial supply chains [07:11, 07:17]. He details ongoing collaborations between researchers, the Department of Commerce, and aerospace manufacturers to build safe emulation testbeds where independent security researchers can responsibly analyze avionics systems without compromising operational air safety [14:29, 21:35]. The address outlines the virtual schedule, research tracks, and interactive challenges, highlighting inclusivity and cross-sector cooperation in strengthening global aviation resilience [28:56, 36:18].

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: MITM: The Mystery in the Middle
talks.teaser: Analyzes security concerns across the Aircraft Information Services Domain, ARINC 821 networking, and Electronic Flight Bags.
talks.summary:
The Aircraft Information Services Domain

The Aircraft Information Services Domain (AISD) serves as a critical intermediary network domain on modern commercial aircraft, bridging flight safety domains with operational and passenger networks.

ARINC 821 Architecture and Interfaces

ARINC 821 defines the networking specifications and protocol standards connecting Electronic Flight Bags (EFBs), Flight Attendant Panels, and maintenance terminals across aircraft systems.

Connected Ground Systems and PKI Implementations

Maintaining secure communications between onboard units and airline ground infrastructure relies on public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates for software updates and telemetry transfers.

Threat Vectors in Cabin and Maintenance Networks

Potential security vulnerabilities exist where portable crew devices, cabin management systems, and maintenance terminals interface with the AISD, requiring strict boundary isolation and message validation.

talks.title: Low Cost VHF Receiver
talks.teaser: Demonstrates how to build an inexpensive multichannel VHF receiver using a Raspberry Pi and RTL-SDR to record ATC audio.
talks.summary:
Recording Air Traffic Control Communications

The OpenSky Network and the EU-funded ATCO2 project developed distributed receiver networks to systematically capture and transcribe Air Traffic Control (ATC) voice communications over VHF frequencies.

The ATCO2 Receiver Feeder Architecture

The project explores how crowdsourced ATC voice recordings uploaded to the OpenSky repository can be processed, archived, and analyzed to improve air traffic management efficiency and safety.

Setting Up the RTLSDR-Airband Receiver

Building a dedicated VHF receiver station utilizes RTLSDR-Airband, an open-source software package capable of simultaneously monitoring multiple AM voice channels across civil aviation bands.

Hardware Assembly on Raspberry Pi

The physical receiver is assembled using a standard Raspberry Pi single-board computer, an inexpensive RTL-SDR USB tuner dongle, and a tuned dipole antenna kit configured for aviation VHF frequencies.

talks.title: Introduction to ACARS
talks.teaser: Introduces the ACARS protocol, demonstrates live message decoding with an RTL-SDR, and reviews risks in CPDLC datalinks.
talks.summary:
Origins and Structure of ACARS

The Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS) evolved from early telex messaging into a standardized digital datalink protocol used across VHF, HF, and SATCOM links.

Capturing and Decoding Transmissions with SDR

Setting up an inexpensive RTL-SDR receiver enables enthusiasts and researchers to intercept unencrypted ACARS transmissions broadcast in plaintext and decode airline operations, weather, and telemetry data.

Vulnerabilities in CPDLC and Data Links

Controller-Pilot Data Link Communications (CPDLC) utilizes ACARS networks to transmit air traffic instructions directly to cockpits. The lack of native authentication introduces risks of spoofed route clearances or message tampering.

The Evolution Toward ACARS Over IP

Modern e-enabled aircraft are transitioning toward internet protocol datalinks, expanding onboard connectivity while requiring modern cryptographic protections to replace legacy broadcast radio architectures.

talks.title: Hacking Airplane A2G Systems
talks.teaser: Analyzes vulnerabilities in airplane air-to-ground communication links using LTE-Advanced and satellite transceivers.
talks.summary:
Air-to-Ground Communication Infrastructure

Modern commercial aircraft rely on Air-to-Ground (A2G) communication systems to transmit flight performance telemetry, airline operational data, and passenger in-flight internet traffic.

Cellular and Satellite Datalink Architecture

A2G networks utilize high-speed LTE-Advanced terrestrial cellular base stations for over-land routes and seamlessly switch to satellite transceivers when operating over oceans or remote regions.

Vulnerability Analysis in A2G Transceivers

Weaknesses in radio link authentication, protocol parsing, and transceiver handoffs present attack vectors for intercepting or disrupting communications between aircraft and ground stations.

Hardening Connected Avionics Components

Securing A2G communications requires robust network segmentation between passenger Wi-Fi gateways and core avionics buses, combined with mutual authentication across all cellular and satellite uplinks.

talks.title: Hackers and ISACs
talks.teaser: Discusses building collaborative relationships and trust between independent security researchers and Aviation ISACs.
talks.summary:
The Role of Independent Aerospace Research

Good-faith vulnerability research provides vital insights into real-world risks across civil aviation, but historic industry tensions have sometimes hindered open collaboration.

Information Sharing and Analysis Centers

Information Sharing and Analysis Centers (ISACs) serve as industry hubs that collect threat intelligence, facilitate vulnerability reporting, and share actionable defenses among airlines and manufacturers.

Bridging the Cultural Divide

Fostering productive relationships between independent hackers and corporate security teams requires transparent communication channels, mutual respect, and clear expectations for disclosure.

Strengthening Coordinated Aviation Security

By learning from past disclosure conflicts, ISACs and researchers can establish durable frameworks that protect safety-critical aerospace infrastructure through coordinated remediation.

talks.title: Hacking Aerospace Cybersecurity Regulation
talks.teaser: Explores legal frameworks, regulatory mandates, and best practices for supporting good-faith cybersecurity research in aviation.
talks.summary:
Cybersecurity in Safety-Critical Aviation

The aerospace sector operates under stringent regulatory oversight where airworthiness certification and physical passenger safety govern all software and hardware engineering.

Adapting Good-Faith Research Models

While commercial software industries have embraced bug bounties and external penetration testing, applying these practices to certified avionics requires navigating complex liability and safety standards.

The Regulatory Role of Aviation Authorities

Federal and international aviation regulators play an essential role in establishing legal safe harbors and compliance frameworks that encourage researchers to disclose findings responsibly.

Developing Future Regulatory Standards

Panelists examine ongoing initiatives to harmonize regulatory mandates with rapid security cycles, ensuring aerospace standards evolve to meet emerging cyber threats without compromising physical safety.

talks.title: GPS Spoofing 101
talks.teaser: Explains the principles of GPS signal manipulation and reviews hands-on spoofing attack scenarios and receiver mitigation techniques.
talks.summary:
Ubiquity of Global Positioning Systems

Civilian Global Positioning System (GPS) signals provide essential positioning, navigation, and precise timing data for autonomous vehicles, unmanned aerial systems, and commercial aircraft.

Mechanics of GPS Signal Spoofing

Unencrypted civilian L1 GPS signals lack cryptographic signatures, allowing attackers using software-defined radios to broadcast slightly higher-power counterfeit signals that gradually hijack receiver tracking loops.

Denial of Service Versus False Coordinates

Attackers can execute denial of service by jamming receiver front-ends or introduce sophisticated drift vectors that misreport vehicle location and velocity without triggering immediate alarms.

State-of-the-Art Mitigation Strategies

Countering GPS spoofing involves deploying multi-antenna beamforming, inertial navigation cross-checks, signal-to-noise monitoring, and upcoming cryptographic authentication standards like Chimera and Galileo OSNMA.

talks.title: Pilot Reactions to Attacks on Avionic Systems
talks.teaser: Evaluates how 30 commercial pilots respond in flight simulators to simulated ADS-B, ACARS, and IFE cyberattacks.
talks.summary:
Theoretical Attacks Versus Operational Reality

While academic researchers have demonstrated technical exploits against ADS-B, ACARS, and in-flight entertainment systems, assessing real-world safety impacts requires evaluating human pilot reactions.

Flight Simulator Study with Commercial Pilots

Researchers conducted controlled experiments using certified commercial flight simulators and thirty type-rated airline pilots to observe responses to unexpected instrument deceptions.

Ghost Targets and False Collision Alerts

Injecting counterfeit traffic alerts tested whether flight crews could identify spurious collision warnings or if deceptive displays compelled pilots to initiate evasive maneuvers.

Landing Guidance Manipulation and Recovery

Simulated spoofing of approach guidance evaluated how flight crews detect deceptive localizer and glide path signals during critical descent phases, emphasizing pilot training and cockpit cross-checks.

talks.title: Exploiting Spacecraft
talks.teaser: Demonstrates command replay, command link intrusion, and GPS jamming attacks against operational spacecraft simulators.
talks.summary:
The Spacecraft Threat Landscape

Space assets increasingly face cyber threats targeting ground stations, satellite communications links, and onboard flight computers controlling mission payloads.

Command Replay and Link Intrusion Attacks

Using high-fidelity spacecraft simulation environments, researchers demonstrated how unauthenticated or weakly protected uplink channels permit command replay attacks and unauthorized command injection.

Denial of Service via GPS Jamming

Simulating localized GPS jamming against spacecraft positioning receivers illustrates how loss of precise timing and orbit determination degrades satellite pointing accuracy and payload functionality.

Defensive Hardening for Space Missions

Mitigating spacecraft exploits requires implementing robust cryptographic authentication on telemetry and telecommand links, securing ground segment control software, and auditing simulated flight hardware.

talks.title: Experimental Aviation Risks and Rewards
talks.teaser: Examines the engineering challenges, risk management decisions, and hacker mindset behind building an experimental homebuilt aircraft.
talks.summary:
The Maker Mindset in Homebuilt Aircraft

Building an experimental aircraft from raw blueprints represents one of the most demanding maker projects, requiring extensive discipline across composite fabrication, avionics wiring, and mechanical assembly.

The AeroCanard and Canard Design Lineage

The AeroCanard FG is a four-seat composite aircraft derived from the Cozy Mark IV and Burt Rutan's pioneering Long-EZ canard design, offering high cruise efficiency and stall-resistant aerodynamics.

Applying Information Risk Principles to Aviation

Evaluating the decision to construct and fly a homebuilt plane through the lens of professional risk management highlights the trade-offs between structural margins, builder expertise, and flight safety.

Managing Engineering Failure Modes

Amateur aircraft builders must establish rigorous quality assurance protocols, inspect avionics power distribution, and verify flight control surfaces to mitigate life-critical failure modes.

talks.title: Dissecting Wireless Privacy in Aviation
talks.teaser: Analyzes how plaintext wireless protocols and crowdsourced sensor networks undermine privacy for corporate, government, and military aircraft.
talks.summary:
Insecurity in Aviation Radio Protocols

Air traffic management systems rely on legacy wireless standards like ADS-B and Mode S that broadcast aircraft identifiers, precise positions, and flight telemetry in unencrypted plaintext.

Crowdsourced Ubiquitous Surveillance

Combining low-cost RTL-SDR receivers with crowdsourced tracking platforms allows global sensor networks to aggregate real-time flight movements without requiring proprietary radar installations.

Tracking Sensitive Corporate and Military Flights

Case studies illustrate how correlating open-source flight telemetry with public corporate registries enables third parties to trace movements of corporate executives, government officials, and military transports.

Limitations of Industry Privacy Initiatives

Efforts to preserve flight privacy through temporary anonymous transponder identifiers struggle against persistent multi-sensor correlation, making meaningful privacy elusive in modern airspace.

talks.title: Deep Space Networking
talks.teaser: Explores communication protocols, extreme latency challenges, and data architectures used in deep space network communications.
talks.summary:
DEF CON Security Research Presentation

This talk covers technical security topics and vulnerability research. The presentation includes discussion of contemporary security challenges, demonstrations of exploitation techniques, and insights into defensive countermeasures and security best practices.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: Cybersecurity & Aviation Regulation
talks.teaser: Examines how aviation standards like DO-178C must adapt to address modern cockpit interfaces, maintenance ports, and connected systems.
talks.summary:
Evolution of Aviation Software Standards

Aviation software certification standards such as DO-178C originated from mechanical component lifecycles, assuming parts remain static after airworthiness inspection and only degrade physically over time.

Connected Cockpits and Changing Threat Models

The introduction of cockpit USB charging ports, crew-carried tablet Electronic Flight Bags, and wireless datalinks challenges legacy assumptions that flight systems remain physically isolated.

Four Critical Aircraft Attack Surfaces

Modern aircraft security centers on four primary vectors: maintenance upload interfaces, passenger entertainment connections, crew-accessible cockpit ports, and pre-flight software verification.

Establishing Post-Installation Integrity Verification

Maintaining long-term airworthiness requires regulatory frameworks that enforce continuous software integrity checks, cryptographic validation of field-loadable software, and rigorous cabin network segmentation.

talks.title: Cybersecurity Lessons Learned in Human Spaceflight
talks.teaser: Draws on human spaceflight missions to highlight software redundancy, access tiering, and command protocol resilience for space systems.
talks.summary:
Critical Space Infrastructure Dependencies

Space assets underpin critical modern infrastructure, supporting global GPS timing, financial transaction validation, worldwide military communications, and weather observation networks.

The End of Security Through Inaccessibility

Historic reliance on orbital physical isolation as a security boundary is no longer tenable as ground station networks, supply chains, and satellite constellations face sophisticated cyber threats.

Software Engineering Standards from Manned Missions

Human spaceflight architectures enforce strict software engineering practices, including near-zero defect tolerances, multi-layered redundant compute clusters, and tiered access permissions.

Securing Commercial and Exploration Missions

As commercial space stations, lunar exploration programs, and international space competitions expand, adopting distributed architectures and robust command protocols is essential to protect mission integrity.

talks.title: Critical Aerospace Cybersecurity
talks.teaser: Shows how red and blue teams collaborate using a hack-and-fix methodology to harden avionics, in-cabin entertainment, and ATM systems.
talks.summary:
Digital Transformation of Modern Aerospace

Modern aircraft cabins increasingly incorporate complex consumer entertainment, passenger Wi-Fi connectivity, and smart devices, significantly expanding the digital attack surface of civil airliners.

The Hack and Fix Testing Methodology

Hardening aerospace systems requires iterative offensive security testing where red teams simulate real-world attacks against avionics, cabin components, and air traffic management networks.

Purple Teaming for Resilient Avionics

Blue teams and red teams work collaboratively across design, integration, and operational phases to detect vulnerabilities early and incorporate remediation directly into airworthiness certification cycles.

Security by Design in Air Traffic Management

Integrating cybersecurity-by-design principles across flight controllers and ground radar networks ensures systems remain robust against tampering while meeting strict civil aviation safety requirements.

talks.title: Building Connections Across the Aviation Ecosystem
talks.teaser: Brings together leaders from government, airlines, and research communities to discuss coordinating IT and OT defense across aviation.
talks.summary:
Coordinating IT and OT Security Across Aviation

Protecting modern civil aviation requires securing an interconnected ecosystem comprising commercial airlines, international airports, air traffic control centers, and third-party supply chain vendors.

Government and Industry Collaboration

Panelists share perspectives from regulatory agencies, aircraft manufacturers, and airport operators on sharing real-time threat intelligence and harmonizing emergency response protocols.

Securing Aviation Supply Chains

Managing cyber risk across distributed aviation suppliers requires continuous oversight of software updates, ground service hardware, and operational technology assets deployed across airport facilities.

Engaging the Security Research Community

The panel highlights actionable avenues for independent cybersecurity researchers to engage constructively with aviation stakeholders to improve collective defense and preserve global aviation safety.

talks.title: Checklist for Aviation Vulnerability Disclosure
talks.teaser: Presents a practical checklist for researchers and aerospace vendors to coordinate vulnerability disclosures smoothly and build trust.
talks.summary:
Challenges of Vulnerability Disclosure in Aviation

Discovering security vulnerabilities in aviation IT and operational flight systems introduces complex legal, safety, and operational considerations that complicate standard disclosure workflows.

Researcher Preparation and Coordination

Security researchers must establish reproducible proof-of-concept demonstrations, document potential safety impacts, and engage trusted coordination intermediaries like Aviation ISACs or CERTs.

Vendor Evaluation and Remediation Steps

Aviation vendors and equipment manufacturers must assess the airworthiness implications of disclosed findings, establish communication timelines, and coordinate firmware fixes across airline fleets.

Building Long-Term Industry Trust

Treating each vulnerability disclosure as an opportunity for institutional learning fosters mutual trust between independent security researchers, airline operators, and regulatory authorities.

talks.title: Breakdown of the FAA Privacy ICAO Address Program
talks.teaser: Analyzes the effectiveness of the FAA's Privacy ICAO Address program against crowdsourced ADS-B aircraft tracking networks.
talks.summary:
The FAA Privacy ICAO Address Program

In January 2020, the Federal Aviation Administration introduced the Privacy ICAO Address (PIA) program to allow general aviation aircraft operators to mask their identity by using temporary randomized hex codes.

Bypassing Masked Identifiers with ADS-B Networks

Despite using randomized ICAO addresses, crowdsourced ADS-B receiver networks can correlate departure airports, flight trajectories, and secondary radio transponder emissions to deanonymize enrolled aircraft.

Quantifying Privacy Loss Through Simulation

A custom privacy simulator models aircraft movements over time, demonstrating that even with expanded operator enrollment, persistent sensor coverage allows adversaries to reconstruct flight histories.

Architectural Solutions for Aviation Privacy

Enhancing the PIA program requires technical modifications, including synchronized dynamic address rotation and cryptographic flight plan authentication to prevent multi-point sensor tracking.

talks.title: Attacking Flight Management Systems
talks.teaser: Uses reverse engineering to uncover vulnerabilities in flight management computers and demonstrates manipulation of navigation data.
talks.summary:
The Critical Role of Flight Management Systems

Flight Management Systems (FMS) automate in-flight navigation, calculate fuel efficiency profiles, generate route plans, and provide lateral and vertical guidance commands directly to the autopilot.

Reverse Engineering FMS Firmware

Researchers reverse-engineered the software and firmware of a widely deployed commercial flight management computer, analyzing how it processes navigation databases and external bus commands.

Manipulating Navigation and Waypoint Databases

Vulnerabilities discovered in the software validation routines allow an attacker to alter stored waypoint coordinates, airway identifiers, and procedural altitude constraints.

Operational Risk Scenarios in Navigation Control

Tampering with flight management data can mislead cockpit navigation displays, degrade autopilot tracking precision, and induce pilot disorientation during instrument approach procedures.

talks.title: General Aviation (GA) Electronic Flight Bags
talks.teaser: Surveys security weaknesses in connected General Aviation Electronic Flight Bag applications and provides mitigation strategies for developers.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Connected Electronic Flight Bags

General aviation pilots increasingly rely on tablet-based Electronic Flight Bags (EFBs) for real-world flight planning, weather updates, aeronautical charts, and weight-and-balance calculations.

Common Vulnerability Classes in EFB Applications

Security assessments across multiple commercial EFB products reveal recurring flaws in insecure API communications, unauthenticated local data storage, and weak cryptographic validation of aeronautical charts.

Risks of Untrusted Data Feeds in Flight Planning

Corrupted navigation data or spoofed weather overlays delivered via insecure cloud backends can mislead pilots during flight preparation or cause situational awareness failures in flight.

Developer Guidance for Hardening EFB Software

Mitigating security risks requires EFB developers to enforce certificate pinning, sanitize external sensor feeds from portable ADS-B receivers, and validate navigation database integrity.

talks.title: A Deeper Dive into ILS and ADS-B Spoofing
talks.teaser: Examines the fundamental protocol weaknesses that enable RF spoofing attacks against Instrument Landing Systems and ADS-B broadcasts.
talks.summary:
Reliance on Unauthenticated Aviation Wireless Protocols

Civil aviation navigation and surveillance protocols were designed decades ago with a focus on signal reliability and availability, omitting modern cryptographic protections.

Mechanics of Instrument Landing System Spoofing

The Instrument Landing System (ILS) utilizes amplitude-modulated VHF and UHF directional radio beams to guide approaching aircraft along the runway localizer and glide path.

Injecting Ghost Aircraft via ADS-B

Because Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) transmissions lack sender authentication, software-defined radios can inject false aircraft tracks with deceptive speeds, altitudes, and callsigns.

Addressing Fundamental Wireless Deficiencies

Mitigating wireless spoofing requires sensor fusion on the aircraft, cross-verifying radio navigation coordinates with optical sensors and radar, and integrating cryptographic message verification.

talks.title: 747 Walkthrough From a Hacker Perspective
talks.teaser: Tours a decommissioned Boeing 747 airframe to examine cockpit systems, avionics bays, and physical attack surfaces.
talks.summary:
Physical Architecture of the Queen of the Skies

A hands-on technical walkthrough of a retired Boeing 747 airframe provides researchers with physical access to explore the architecture of classic widebody jetliners.

Avionics Bay Layout and System Busses

Examining the main electronics equipment (MEC) bay reveals the physical layout of Line Replaceable Units (LRUs), ARINC wire bundles, and navigation computers beneath the cockpit floor.

Cockpit Displays and Flight Deck Controls

The tour highlights pilot interface controls, flight director panels, and the physical isolation mechanisms implemented between navigation controls and external data ports.

Mapping the Physical and Electronic Attack Surface

Analyzing physical access paths, maintenance access panels, and wired sensor connections illustrates how hardware security controls function across operational airframes.

talks.title: Airport Hacking Choose Your Own Adventure
talks.teaser: Navigates through airport check-in systems, digital signage, retail networks, and logistics infrastructure to illustrate facility security risks.
talks.summary:
The Airport as an Interconnected Smart City

Modern commercial airports operate as complex municipal ecosystems integrating passenger check-in kiosks, baggage handling conveyors, retail payment terminals, and security screening infrastructure.

Threat Vectors in Passenger and Facility Networks

Shared network backbones connecting public flight information display systems (FIDS), automated gate signage, and airline ticketing terminals present targets for ransomware and lateral traversal.

Supply Chain and Multi-Stakeholder Logistics

Airport operations depend on fragmented municipal, federal, and third-party commercial contracts, creating security gaps where point-of-sale systems interface with airport utility controls.

Real-World Incident Analysis and Mitigation

Examining publicly documented security incidents underscores the critical necessity for network micro-segmentation, robust incident response planning, and vendor security oversight across airport facilities.

talks.title: Airport Hacking Choose Your Own Adventure
talks.teaser: Explores security pitfalls across passenger terminals, baggage handling, gate signage, and airline check-in infrastructure.
talks.summary:

Modern commercial airports operate as complex municipal ecosystems integrating passenger check-in kiosks, baggage handling conveyors, retail payment terminals, and security screening infrastructure.

Threat Vectors in Passenger and Facility Networks

Shared network backbones connecting public flight information display systems (FIDS), automated gate signage, and airline ticketing terminals present targets for ransomware and lateral traversal.

Supply Chain and Multi-Stakeholder Logistics

Real-World Incident Analysis and Mitigation

Examining publicly documented security incidents underscores the critical necessity for network micro-segmentation, robust incident response planning, and vendor security oversight across airport facilities.
